keybind.showHint: Hover your token (or select one) and press to get a card for everyone you know who is in sight — their token art, the word, their name, your notes. Press again to sweep them away. Drag a card to keep it: dragged cards stay put, stay wired to their token, and close only with their ✕.
keybind.oneHint: One connection instead of the whole web. SELECT your own token, HOVER the person you're asking about, and press: you get that single card. Press again while still hovering them to close it, or move to somebody else to open theirs. Needs both — a selection for who is asking and a hover for who is being asked about.
keybind.describeHint: Hover a token and press for a card with their art and their written description — who this person is, rather than who they know. Press again on the same person to close it, or move to somebody else to swap. GM only: it reads the actor's private biography, which is your prep, not the table's.
keybind.addHint: Hover someone and press. The token you hover becomes the person the tie is TO, and you pick whose list it goes on — unless they are the only character you can write on, in which case it becomes the person the tie is FROM and you pick who it is to. Right-click cannot do this: Foundry only opens a token's HUD for its owner, so a player right-clicking an NPC gets nothing.
keybind.knownHint: Hover a creature or a person and press. Their page in your character's notebook opens — the Known tab on your sheet — started for you if you have never written about them before. Three tokens of the same goblin are one page. Whose notebook it is: the token you have selected, else the character you are assigned, else the only one you own here. A token you cannot see cannot be written down.
keybind.inspect: Take a closer look at the hovered creature
keybind.inspectHint: Hover anyone and press to look them over — the only thing that starts an identification check. Nothing is ever rolled automatically.

settings.sheetTab: Show the Ties tab on actor sheets
settings.sheetTabHint: Adds a Ties tab to actor sheets. The tab is written against the default dnd5e sheet; a module that replaces the sheet entirely may render it oddly or not at all. Turn this off if so — the header button opens the same editor anywhere.
settings.playerAccess: Let players see their own ties
settings.playerAccessHint: Players can show the ties of a character they own, and read and edit the Ties tab on that character's sheet — including its notes, which are their character's own. They only ever see their own connections, and only ones their token can actually see: walls and light are respected. Turn this off to make the whole feature GM-only again.
settings.nearDistanceHint: Within this many squares a card simply sits over its token. Beyond it, a thin line is also drawn from you to them, so a card floating across the map still belongs to somebody.
settings.holdDefault: Hold every reveal for my approval
settings.holdDefaultHint: When a player's study check lands, park what they learned and ask you before it reaches their notebook — so a good roll can cue a scene instead of a paragraph appearing mid-sentence. There is no deny: the prompt's Later just leaves it pending, and it stays deliverable from game.pentaryn.ties.study.pending() for as long as you like. Individual creatures can override this either way.
settings.advantageStackingHint: How this module combines advantage and disadvantage on the checks it makes. The 2024 rules cancel them out whenever both are present, however many there are.
settings.advantageNet: Count them up, the majority wins
